kind: daily edition: news from 15 and early 16 October not yet on the wire, plus re-checks of earlier stories whose primary had not been fetched

latest_release.title: Daily edition, 16 October: AI safety incidents go on the record
latest_release.summary: Eighteen new stories from 15 and early 16 October. Lead: the FTC has served civil investigative demands on OpenAI and Anthropic seeking records on safety incidents, safeguards and privacy policies; an FTC spokesperson confirmed them to CBS (gov-18). The same day the White House AI task force adopted its charter and asked for protocols for labs to report breaches (gov-19, Semafor only), and the FSB's own pages are now the primary for its final AI practices (gov-14, updated). Worth your attention: the Aoki infostealer now steals Claude, Codex, Cursor and Copilot tokens from developer machines (sec-30); Next.js fixed two critical unauthenticated RCEs (sec-29); 'PwnEscape' leaked host memory from Vercel's sandboxes, though NVD has no entry yet for its CVE id (sec-31); CISA added Atlassian Data Center CVE-2026-21589 to KEV (sec-26); Meta's Muse Spark Open licence treats models improved with its outputs as derivatives (oss-17); Accenture caps centrally funded Claude use at $29 a head (biz-25, single source); Cohere plans to buy AISLE (biz-23). Deadlines: CISA's federal deadline for the Windows Shell and Ivanti flaws is today, 16 October; Cisco CVE-2026-76519, PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 and the Ahsay flaws are due 17 October; Atlassian CVE-2026-21589 is reportedly due 18 October; Oracle's Critical Patch Update is due 20 October; the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill's Lords report stage is provisionally 26 October; objections in the Character.AI sale are due 30 October; Meta's answers to the senators are due 31 October; the ICO agentic-AI call for evidence closes 20 November; Gemini 4 Argon's introductory price ends 30 November; OpenAI removes GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 from its API on 14 January 2027. Twenty earlier stories whose primary was not fetched were re-checked: new primaries for gov-14 and sec-25, and notes or corrections on biz-19 (Axios says 'cash flow positive', not adjusted profit), ai-17, ai-05, sec-08, gov-06, biz-18, biz-03, biz-04 and biz-09; developments on sec-11 (about 700 French stores), sec-22, sec-23, biz-02 and gov-07. An independent verifier on a different model checked all 34 new or updated stories and its 24 fixes are applied (data/factcheck-2026-10-16.json). Your lane was not read, so your wire decisions are still not reflected.

stories.headline: Financial Stability Board finalises AI guidance for banks; Reuters says it calls for more human oversight of agentic AI and risk-based approval triggers

changes.what: Development: FSB primary fetched. The press release 'FSB finalises sound practices for the responsible adoption of AI' (https://www.fsb.org/2026/10/fsb-finalises-sound-practices-for-the-responsible-adoption-of-artificial-intelligence-ai/) and the final report page (https://www.fsb.org/2026/10/sound-practices-for-responsible-adoption-of-artificial-intelligence-ai-final-report/) are both dated 15 Oct. They set out 12 sound practices in two groups: board/senior-management governance and lifecycle risk management (use-case materiality, data, explainability, performance monitoring, human oversight, cyber/ICT, third-party/concentration risk). The report page names GenAI and agentic AI as drivers. Practice 10 ties human oversight to the risk, autonomy and complexity of each use case. The practices are non-binding and adaptable, and the FSB will update them as the technology evolves. They were delivered to the 15 Oct G20 FMCBG meeting with Chair Andrew Bailey's letter (https://www.fsb.org/2026/10/fsb-chair-sets-out-fsb-work-on-ai-and-stablecoins/, 12 Oct), which flags AI-related risks. Caveat: the press release itself does not mention agentic AI. That language appears only on the report page.

Re-check: the FSB primary was fetched (press release https://www.fsb.org/2026/10/fsb-finalises-sound-practices-for-the-responsible-adoption-of-artificial-intelligence-ai/ and final report page, both 15 Oct) and is now the primary; Reuters moves to coverage. The quote is now from the FSB report (it was the Reuters line 'AI agents do not reason like humans and may interpret pre-defined goals in unexpected ways.'). The press release does not mention agentic AI; the approval-trigger and 'synthetic employees' details were not on the fetched pages (the full PDF was not read) and are attributed to Reuters.

Fact-check: the headline now attributes 'agentic AI' and 'approval triggers' to Reuters; 'non-binding' is not FSB wording for the final practices. Bailey's 12 Oct letter describes the practices as finalised before the 15 Oct publication.
